name: m5-hashseed-pickler-prof20

variantDescriptions.seed10: `-Dscalac.hashSeed=10`: symbol, tree, `TypeVar` and `Scope` hashes from per-run ids scrambled with the seed; a typical layout (88.89G instructions/op, 2 forks within 0.07%)
variantDescriptions.seed20: `-Dscalac.hashSeed=20`: symbol, tree, `TypeVar` and `Scope` hashes from per-run ids scrambled with the seed; the pathological layout (99.17G instructions/op, +11.6%, and 4103.6 vs 4002 MB/op allocated, in both forks)

description: Why does one hash layout cost 12% more? In `m5-hashseed-pickler-xbatch-many` (`-Xbatch`, `-Ystop-after:pickler`, strong chunked uniques, fixed young gen), 21 of 22 seeds fell within 88.0–89.7G instructions/op, but seed 20 took 99.17G and allocated 100 MB/op more, in both forks, with identical compiler output (same symbol and unique-type counts) and an unremarkable uniques table (max probe 38). Profiles of instructions, cycles (kperf) and allocation, and a JIT recording, for seed 20 against the typical seed 10, 2 forks each, to find the hash-sensitive structure.
